                                     PROJECT NO. 59142


REVIEW OF ERCOT’S                              §    PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
INTERCONNECTION PROCESSES                      §
FOR LARGE LOADS                                §                  OF TEXAS




                             COMMENTS OF
          NIGHTPEAK ENERGY LLC ON MAY 6TH STAFF MEMORANDUM
               FILED BY THE DEPUTY EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR


Nightpeak Energy LLC (“Nightpeak”) files these comments on the Deputy Executive Director’s
Memorandum filed on May 6, 2026, regarding Batch Zero Entry Criteria. Our comments are
focused on the Base Case group identified in the Table contained in the Memorandum.

Nightpeak is a power plant owner operator and early-stage data center developer. We locate the
data centers we develop adjacent or near to our power plants to ensure that data centers don’t
negatively impact local grid reliability and have access to dispatchable power. We are currently
actively developing a two-phase data center adjacent to a power plant we are developing.

Nightpeak appreciates the opportunity to file these brief comments on the May 6th Staff
Memorandum. While these comments are primarily focused on the requirements in this
memorandum, it is our understanding that this memo will set new standards, upon PUCT
approval, which will be incorporated into the new ERCOT Batch Study Protocols. Our
comments will focus on these issues from the Table –

   1) Additional Evidence of Project Maturity – In the Advancing column the issuance of a
      notice to proceed (NTP) construction to the utility is a criterion that carries great
      significance as at that point a project has satisfied significant financial obligations to
      proceed with the interconnection. This criterion should also be in the Developing column
      as well.

   2) Additional Evidence of Project Maturity – In the Developing column there is a
      requirement that there needs to be a contract for the general contractor and the substation
      contractor. A contract with a General Contractor and a contract with the Substation
      Contractor are substantial project milestones with major commitments from the developer
      so requiring both contracts is not necessary. Nightpeak recommends that the PUCT
      accept a revision that replaces “and” with “or”. The table is attached with our proposed
      language changes.




                                                1
 Respectfully Submitted,


/s/ Greg Blue___________________
